title: Bottle opener
prompt: a bottle opener hooked under a capped bottle on a table with three buttons: “Hook” seats the lip beneath the cap; “Lift” raises the handle and peels the cap upward; “Reset” replaces the cap; see-through reveals the contact fulcrum and the short load arm beneath the cap
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Levers
blurb: A crown-cap opener multiplies a lift of the handle, staged on a table with cap replacement as a teaching control.

identity.note: Levers / Levers in action / Second-class levers / Bottle opener, page 22. Raising the handle overcomes cap resistance between cap-top support and effort.
identity.classificationNote: A named machine or diagram inside Levers is not a separate main chapter. The parking-meter heading is historical.

adaptationDecision.reason: Distinct from the cleared can-opener, which cuts and feeds around a tin rim with wheels and gears. Shares second-class force multiplication with nutcrackers but acts on a cap edge.

prompt.note: Faithful for the pictured crown-cap opener. One contact supports the tool on the cap and its lip lifts the cap edge. Reset explicitly replaces the cap as a teaching action. A screw cap or corkscrew would be another mechanism.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Bench or scale teaching adaptation of a named book example. Controls, fixtures and test specimens stage the lesson and are not claimed as the book apparatus.

representativeConstruction.usedFor: The mechanical description of a cap-top fulcrum and a hook under the crimped skirt only. No electronics, camera or powered parts are used.
representativeConstruction.bookEvidence: 1998 and 2016 printed page 22 support the second-class lever action. The 2016 scan image and saved OCR from both editions were read for this build.

steps: Hook slides the lifting lip under the crown-cap skirt while the far bearing rests on the top.
Lift rotates the tool at the cap-top contact, peeling the near edge upward and freeing the crimp from the bottle bead.
The released cap clears the head sideways and falls onto the table.
Reset replaces the specimen with a fresh capped bottle and returns the opener. It does not reseal a used cap.
teachingAdaptations: Enlarged representative opener with coloured grip, empty specimen bottle and tabletop.
Controls supply the implied hand effort. The bottle is assumed held steady by the user.
Coloured contact dots and bracket lines are teaching overlays, excluded from anatomy.
The short bracket spans bearing to hooked lip. The long bracket spans bearing to the hand position.
Prescribed cap peel and falling trajectory demonstrate the mechanism and do not predict material forces.
